idempotency: A guarantee that retrying the same operation does not create an additional side effect.
workload identity: A verifiable identity for software or an agent, distinct from the human or system that initiated the work.
prompt injection: Untrusted text that attempts to override the system’s instructions or induce an unauthorised action.
N-run reliability: The rate at which a system reaches an acceptable outcome across repeated runs of the same scenario.
policy-as-code: Rules expressed in a machine-evaluable form that can be versioned, tested, and enforced.
HITL: Human in the loop: a person must approve or contribute before the system continues.
HOTL: Human on the loop: the system can act, while a person supervises and can intervene.
entitlements: The data and actions an identity is permitted to access.
lineage: Evidence showing where data came from and how it changed on the way to an output.
semantic layer: A governed business vocabulary that keeps entity and metric definitions consistent across systems.
sandbox escape: A failure in which code or a tool crosses the isolation boundary intended to contain it.
canary release: A release made available to a limited share of traffic first so evidence can be gathered before wider rollout.
attack success rate: The share of adversarial test attempts that achieve the attacker’s defined objective.
token budget: A hard ceiling on the model input and output tokens a task or step may consume.
